mainTopic: Whether an עשיר may set his שבת residence by foot: רב נחמן vs. רב חסדא on the מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the proofs for רב נחמן, and רב's ruling like רבי יהודה
overview: The משנה speaks of a person who sets his שבת residence by going to a spot and declaring it, instead of placing bread there. רבי מאיר says only a poor man (עני) may do this. רבי יהודה says a rich man (עשיר) may too. רב נחמן explains that they argue about saying 'במקומי' (right where I stand), and that everyone agrees naming a distant spot ('במקום פלוני') works only for an עני. רב חסדא reverses this: they argue about 'במקום פלוני', and everyone agrees 'במקומי' works for all. For each view, the גמרא shows which lines of the משנה follow which תנא. A ברייתא supports רב נחמן. It includes רבי יהודה's story of poor people from כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה who spent nightfall at the edge of the תחום so they could collect food in ארומא. רב אשי adds a proof from another משנה: a traveler who was turned back may go, but the townspeople may not. This shows that even רבי יהודה limits 'במקום פלוני' to an עני. רב then rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, and the amud ends by opening a story about רבה בר רב חנן's trips to פומבדיתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן: רבי מאיר limits the foot-עירוב to a poor man
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רב נחמן's explanation of רבי מאיר. Since bread is the main עירוב, the foot-עירוב is only a special leniency for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only for a poor man that the רבנן were lenient. But a rich man may not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: We join רב נחמן mid-sentence as he explains רבי מאיר's opinion. The leniency of making an עירוב just by standing somewhere and declaring it applies only to an עני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, רב נחמן said רבי מאיר holds עיקר עירוב בפת (the main method of עירוב is bread). If bread is the normal method, then declaring 'במקומי' without bread is a special break. The רבנן gave that break only to a poor traveler who has no bread with him. An עשיר, who has bread at home, must use the normal method.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person; here, a traveler without food on hand
A wealthy person; here, someone at home who has bread
They were lenient
The Sages / Rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a brand-new opinion. It is the second half of רב נחמן's statement, which began on the previous amud. The reasoning 'bread is the main עירוב' comes from that earlier part.

phrases.english: It is a poor man for whom the Rabbis were lenient,
phrases.notes: Because for רבי מאיר bread is the main עירוב, the foot method is only a leniency.

phrases.english: but a rich man — no.
phrases.notes: A rich man must make his עירוב with bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָנִי הוּא דְּאַקִּילוּ רַבָּנַן עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן's explanation of רבי מאיר, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן, רבי מאיר holds that 'במקומי' without bread works only for an עני, not an עשיר.

steps.title: רב נחמן: רבי יהודה says the foot-עירוב is the main method
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds the main עירוב is by foot, so declaring 'במקומי' works for both rich and poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds that the main form of עירוב is by foot, so it applies equally to a poor man and a rich man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן now explains the other side of the argument. רבי יהודה treats the foot-עירוב as the basic, original method, so anyone may use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תנאים disagree about which method is the 'real' עירוב. רבי מאיר says bread is primary and foot is a leniency. רבי יהודה says foot is primary and bread is the add-on. Since the foot method is the basic one for רבי יהודה, it is open to an עשיר as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The primary / original form of עירוב
By foot: physically being at the spot and declaring residence there
Holds / is of the opinion

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
the main form of eiruv is by foot,
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of רבי מאיר's view that bread is primary.

phrases.english: so it applies equally to a poor man and a rich man.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: עִיקַּר עֵירוּב בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the מחלוקת under רב נחמן's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן, רבי יהודה holds that 'במקומי' works for both עני and עשיר, because the foot-עירוב is the primary method.

steps.title: רב נחמן: everyone agrees 'at such-and-such place' is only for a poor man
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the argument to 'במקומי'. When someone names a distant spot ('במקום פלוני'), both תנאים agree it works only for an עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said 'my residence is at such-and-such place', everyone agrees: a poor man, yes; a rich man, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן marks the boundary of the argument. In the 'במקום פלוני' case there is no dispute at all: only a poor man may do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a distant place is neither bread nor true 'by foot', since he is not standing there. So even רבי יהודה, who extends the foot-עירוב to the rich, agrees it is only a leniency for the poor. That leaves the whole מחלוקת resting on 'במקומי'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'At such-and-such place': naming a spot where one is not currently standing
Everyone agrees
Yes

steps.whyThisMatters: This boundary is exactly what רב חסדא will reverse in step 7. Keep both cases ('במקומי' and 'במקום פלוני') clearly separate in your mind.

phrases.english: But if he said 'at such-and-such place' —
phrases.notes: A place he is not currently standing in.

phrases.english: everyone agrees:
a poor man, yes; a rich man, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limits of the argument just described in steps 1-2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב נחמן, all agree that 'במקום פלוני' works only for an עני.

steps.title: 'And this is what they said' is taught by רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins fitting the משנה's lines into רב נחמן's model. The phrase 'וזו היא שאמרו' (that a poor man makes an עירוב with his feet) belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who teaches the line 'And this is what they said'? רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא is speaking in the משנה's line 'וזו היא שאמרו: העני מערב ברגליו', and answers that it is רבי מאיר. This is the start of mapping the משנה onto רב נחמן's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That line speaks only of a poor man, which matches רבי מאיר's view that the foot-עירוב is a leniency for the עני alone. So under רב נחמן, this anonymous line of the משנה follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what they said': a line in the משנה
Who teaches it? (Which תנא is speaking?)

phrases.english: 'And this is what they said'
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה: 'a poor man makes an עירוב with his feet'.

phrases.english: who teaches it?
Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹ הִיא שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב נחמן's model to the wording of the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר, since the line restricts the foot-עירוב to the poor.

steps.title: That line refers back to the case of one unfamiliar with a landmark or the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The 'וזו היא שאמרו' line points back to the case of someone who did not know a landmark or the הלכה and said 'במקומי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which case is it referring to? To 'he is not familiar with a landmark, or is not expert in the הלכה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies which earlier case in the משנה 'this is what they said' refers to. It is the 'במקומי' case of a traveler who did not know a landmark or the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רב נחמן perfectly. For him the argument is about 'במקומי', and the 'not familiar / not expert' case is exactly where the traveler says 'במקומי'. So רבי מאיר's 'only a poor man' applies to that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Which clause does it refer to?
He is not familiar (with a landmark)
Expert in the הלכה

phrases.english: And to which clause does it refer?
To 'he is not familiar' (with a landmark)
'or is not expert in the halacha'.
phrases.notes: In that case he says 'במקומי' and acquires 2000 אמות in every direction.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַהֵיָיא קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the mapping by identifying which clause the line modifies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does 'וזו היא שאמרו' refer to?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'אינו מכיר או שאינו בקי בהלכה' case, where he says 'במקומי'.

steps.title: 'They only said bread to be lenient' is taught by רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The line 'ולא אמרו מערבין בפת אלא להקל' belongs to רבי יהודה, who treats bread as an added leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who teaches 'They only said one makes an עירוב with bread in order to be lenient'? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes mapping the משנה. The closing line, which calls bread merely a leniency, follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bread is only a leniency, then the foot method is the primary one. That is exactly רבי יהודה's view under רב נחמן. The bread was given so a rich man does not have to go out and walk to make his עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: One makes an עירוב with bread
To be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: Under רב נחמן: the argument is about 'במקומי'. רבי מאיר says bread is primary, so only a poor man may use the foot method. רבי יהודה says foot is primary, so everyone may. 'במקום פלוני' is only for a poor man, according to all. In the משנה, 'וזו היא שאמרו' is רבי מאיר and 'ולא אמרו... אלא להקל' is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: 'And they only said one makes an eiruv with bread
in order to be lenient'
phrases.notes: Lenient on the rich man, so he need not go out on foot.

phrases.english: who teaches it?
Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ מְעָרְבִין בְּפַת אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the mapping of the משנה under רב נחמן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא authored 'ולא אמרו מערבין בפת אלא להקל'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who holds the foot method is primary and bread is a leniency.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the dispute is about 'at such-and-such place'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees with רב נחמן. The argument is about 'במקום פלוני': רבי מאיר allows it only for a poor man, while רבי יהודה allows it for rich and poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: the dispute is about 'at such-and-such place'. רבי מאיר holds: a poor man yes, a rich man no. רבי יהודה holds: poor and rich alike.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא offers a completely different reading of the משנה. He moves the argument from the 'במקומי' case to the 'במקום פלוני' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, everyone agreed 'במקום פלוני' was only for the poor. For רב חסדא, that exact case is where the two תנאים argue. רבי יהודה lets even an עשיר name a distant place.

keyTerms.meaning: The dispute
An אמורא who argues with רב נחמן here

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two אמוראים. רב נחמן says the argument is about 'במקומי'. רב חסדא says it is about 'במקום פלוני'. Each one says everyone agrees on the other case, but they agree in opposite directions.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
the dispute is about 'at such-and-such place',
for Rabbi Meir holds:
a poor man, yes; a rich man, no,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds:
poor and rich alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רב נחמן's reading by moving the מחלוקת to the 'במקום פלוני' case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב חסדא, for 'במקום פלוני' רבי מאיר allows only an עני, while רבי יהודה allows both.

steps.title: רב חסדא: everyone agrees 'in my place' works for rich and poor
steps.stepSummary: Under רב חסדא, both תנאים agree that saying 'במקומי' works for everyone, because all hold the foot-עירוב is primary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said 'in my place', everyone agrees it works for poor and rich alike, because the main form of עירוב is by foot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his view by stating the case where there is no argument. 'במקומי' works for anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב חסדא holds that even רבי מאיר agrees the foot-עירוב is primary. That is the opposite of how רב נחמן described רבי מאיר. As a result, standing in place and declaring residence is valid for an עשיר as well. The only open question is a distant spot.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In my place': where one is currently standing

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: the argument is about 'במקומי', and all agree 'במקום פלוני' is for the poor only. רב חסדא: the argument is about 'במקום פלוני', and all agree 'במקומי' works for everyone because עיקר עירוב ברגל.

phrases.english: But if he said 'in my place',
everyone agrees:
poor and rich alike,
because the main form of eiruv is by foot.
phrases.notes: For רב חסדא, even רבי מאיר agrees to this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בִּמְקוֹמִי דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's view by stating the case everyone agrees on.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב חסדא, 'במקומי' is valid for both עני and עשיר according to all, since עיקר עירוב ברגל.

steps.title: Under רב חסדא, 'And this is what they said' is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: According to רב חסדא, the line 'וזו היא שאמרו' (a poor man makes an עירוב with his feet) is taught by רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And this is what they said': who teaches it? רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reads the משנה's lines according to רב חסדא, just as it did earlier for רב נחמן. It starts by saying the 'poor man' line comes from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב חסדא, only רבי מאיר limits 'במקום פלוני' to a poor man. רבי יהודה allows it for rich and poor alike. So a line that singles out the poor man must belong to רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And this is what they said', the משנה's line about a poor man making an עירוב with his feet
Who teaches it? (asks which תנא's view a line follows)
A poor man

phrases.english: "And this is what they said"
who teaches it?
Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: Same answer as under רב נחמן, but for a different reason: for רב חסדא, the argument is about 'במקום פלוני'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹ הִיא שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts fitting the משנה into רב חסדא's model from Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'poor man' line follows רבי מאיר

steps.title: Under רב חסדא, the line refers to the traveler caught by nightfall
steps.stepSummary: Under רב חסדא, 'וזו היא שאמרו' points back to the case of 'מי שבא בדרך וחשכה', the traveler who named a specific spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which case does it refer to? To this one: 'one who was coming along the road and it grew dark.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies which case in the משנה the 'poor man' line explains. Under רב חסדא, it is the traveler who was caught by nightfall on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב נחמן (Step 5), the line pointed to the person who said 'במקומי'. Under רב חסדא, everyone agrees that 'במקומי' works for all people. So the line must point to the traveler naming a specific place ('במקום פלוני'), which רבי מאיר allows only for such a person. For רבי יהודה, even someone at home could do this.

keyTerms.meaning: Which case does it stand on, i.e., refer back to?
One who was traveling and night fell (שבת began)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 5. Under רב נחמן, the line pointed to the 'במקומי' case. Under רב חסדא, it points to the traveler case.

phrases.english: And to which case is it referring?
To this one:
"One who was coming along the road and it grew dark."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַהֵיָיא קָאֵי אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues Step 9 by identifying the case the line refers to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to the traveler caught by nightfall

steps.title: Under רב חסדא, 'bread is only a leniency' is agreed by all
steps.stepSummary: Under רב חסדא, the line 'ולא אמרו מערבין בפת אלא להקל' is the view of everyone, not only רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They only said one makes an עירוב with bread as a leniency': who teaches it? Everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assigns the last line of the משנה. Under רב חסדא, both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה agree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב נחמן (Step 6), this line was only רבי יהודה's, because only he held that the foot-עירוב is primary. Under רב חסדא, both תנאים hold the foot-עירוב is primary (Step 8). So both can say that bread is just an added leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: One makes an עירוב using bread
To be lenient, to make things easier
The view of everyone, agreed by all

steps.whatToRemember: The two models read the same משנה differently. רב נחמן: the 'poor man' line is רבי מאיר's and refers to 'במקומי', while the 'bread is a leniency' line is רבי יהודה's. רב חסדא: the 'poor man' line is רבי מאיר's and refers to the traveler, while the 'bread is a leniency' line is agreed by all.

phrases.english: "And they only said one makes an eiruv with bread to be lenient"
who teaches it?
It is the view of everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ מְעָרְבִין בְּפַת אֶלָּא לְהָקֵל מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the fitting of the משנה into רב חסדא's model
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'bread is a leniency' line is agreed by both תנאים

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא matches רב נחמן. In it, רבי מאיר says a rich man must use bread and cannot go out and say 'שביתתי במקומי'. The foot-עירוב is only for the traveler.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports רב נחמן: Both a poor man and a rich man make an עירוב with bread. A rich man may not go out past the תחום and say 'My resting place is where I stand'. This is because the foot-עירוב was only allowed for one who was traveling when night fell. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב נחמן's version of the argument. This step quotes the first half of it: רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the argument is about saying 'במקומי'. Here רבי מאיר explicitly forbids a rich man from saying 'שביתתי במקומי'. That fits רב נחמן and goes against רב חסדא, who said everyone allows 'במקומי'.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in support of him
A rich man
'My שבת resting place is where I am standing'
The שבת boundary of 2000 אמות
By foot, i.e., by walking there in person

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is direct textual support for רב נחמן against רב חסדא about what the תנאים actually argued over.

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav Nachman:
Both a poor man and a rich man
make an eiruv with bread,
and a rich man may not go out beyond the boundary
and say: "My resting place is in my place"
because they only said one makes an eiruv by foot
for one who was coming on the road and it grew dark,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רב חסדא's model and brings support for רב נחמן
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's claim that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about saying 'במקומי'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי מאיר forbids a rich man from saying 'שביתתי במקומי'

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says rich and poor alike may make a foot-עירוב by saying 'תהא שביתתי במקומי'. That is the main form of עירוב, and sending bread through an agent is a leniency for the homeowner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Both a poor man and a rich man make an עירוב by foot. A rich man may go out past the תחום and say 'Let my resting place be where I stand'. This is the main form of עירוב. The חכמים allowed a homeowner to send his עירוב through his servant, his son, or his agent, to make it easier for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי יהודה's side, and it matches רב נחמן's version exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה explicitly allows a rich man to say 'במקומי'. So the argument is precisely about 'במקומי', as רב נחמן said. He also calls the foot-עירוב the 'עיקר', while bread sent through others is only an added convenience.

keyTerms.meaning: The main, original form of the עירוב
Homeowner, a settled (often wealthy) person
His agent, messenger

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עָנִי וְאֶחָד עָשִׁיר מְעָרְבִין בָּרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: Both a poor man and a rich man make an eiruv by foot,
and a rich man may go out beyond the boundary
and say: "Let my resting place be in my place,"
and this is the main form of eiruv.
And the Sages permitted a homeowner
to send his eiruv in the hand of his servant,
in the hand of his son, in the hand of his agent,
in order to be lenient with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֶחָד עָנִי וְאֶחָד עָשִׁיר מְעָרְבִין בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the opposing view
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's model of the מחלוקת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה in the ברייתא explicitly allows a rich man to say 'במקומי'

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story of the poor people coming for food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells how poor people from כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה stood at the תחום at nightfall, then came early the next morning to collect figs and raisins in ארומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a story with the families of בית ממל and בית גוריון in ארומא. They used to hand out dried figs and raisins to poor people in famine years. The poor of כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה would come and be at the edge of the תחום when night fell. The next day they would get up early and come.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה brings a real-life story as proof for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor people did not leave bread. They stood at the edge of their boundary at nightfall, which acquired their שבת resting place there by foot. That let them walk into ארומא the next morning. This shows a foot-עירוב made by declaring 'במקומי' works.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an actual incident brought as proof
Dried figs and raisins
Years of famine or drought
They waited at the boundary until nightfall

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא supports רב נחמן. רבי מאיר says only a traveler can make a foot-עירוב, so a rich man uses bread. רבי יהודה says anyone can declare 'במקומי', and he proves it from the poor people of כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with the members of the Memel household
and the members of the Guryon household in Aroma
who would distribute dried figs and raisins
to the poor in years of famine,
and the poor of the village of Shichin would come
and the poor of the village of Chananya,
and they would wait until nightfall at the boundary;
the next day they would rise early and come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאַנְשֵׁי בֵּית מֶמֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה supports his own view in the ברייתא with a story
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that anyone can make a foot-עירוב by declaring 'במקומי'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of the poor of כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's wording supports רב נחמן. He quotes the case of a man who set out for a city and was turned back by his friend. That man may go, but the rest of the townspeople may not, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: if someone set out to go to a city for which people make an עירוב, and his friend turned him back, he is allowed to go, and all the other people of the town are forbidden. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins a proof for רב נחמן by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the proof. The explanation of why the משנה supports רב נחמן comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far, the ברייתא with רבי מאיר supported רב נחמן. Now רב אשי adds that a משנה points the same way. In the משנה, the traveler and the townspeople get different results, and that difference will be the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה is also precise (it supports this view)
Since it teaches
And his friend turned him back
A city people make an עירוב to reach on שבת

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The Mishnah is also precise (this way),
for it teaches:
One who set out to go
to a city for which an eruv is made,
and his friend turned him back —
he is permitted to go,
and all the people of the town are forbidden,
phrases.notes: The other townspeople may not go to that city on Shabbat.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source, this time a משנה, supporting רב נחמן's position from Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that even רבי יהודה agrees 'במקום פלוני' works only for an עני (against רב חסדא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the man who set out and was turned back by his friend

steps.title: Recalling the question: why is he different from them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier discussion of this משנה. It had asked why the man who set out may go while the other townspeople may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What is different about him, and what is different about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a question it already asked about this משנה. This sets up the answer that will show the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone in the town lives in the same place, so why should one man get a better result? The question forces us to find something special about the man who set out.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (earlier)
What is different?
He / they

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is different about him
and what is different about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא אִיהוּ וּמַאי שְׁנָא אִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Recalls an earlier question about the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes the man who set out different from the other townspeople?

steps.title: רב הונא: the man has two houses far apart
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the משנה deals with a man who owns two houses, with two שבת limits (4,000 אמות) between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: What case are we dealing with here? One where he has two houses, with two שבת limits between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls רב הונא's answer, which describes the exact case in the משנה. The next step will explain why this case makes the man different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man is headed from one house to his other house. His trip is not a short visit. He really left home to go somewhere else, and that detail sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Two שבת limits (4,000 אמות)
Houses

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
What are we dealing with here —
a case where he has two houses,
and two Shabbat limits between them.
phrases.notes: 4,000 אמות: one house in each city.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question from Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man has two houses, two תחומים apart, and he was traveling from one to the other.

steps.title: The traveler counts as poor, the townspeople as rich
steps.stepSummary: Because the man went out on the road, he counts as an עני. The townspeople, who stayed home, count as עשירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for him, since he went out on the road, he counts as a poor man. And these others are rich people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his answer by explaining why the man and the townspeople are treated differently. The man is like an עני, and the others are like עשירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'poor' and 'rich' are not about money. A person on the road has no bread available, so he is like an עני and may set his resting place just by speaking. The people at home have food, so they are like עשירים and need to place bread to make an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he went out on the road
A poor person (here: someone on the road without bread at hand)
Rich people (here: people at home with food)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take 'עני' and 'עשיר' to mean poor and rich with money. The man owns two houses! He is called an עני only because he was out on the road and had no bread to set down.

phrases.english: He, since he went out on the road —
he becomes a poor man.
And these (others) — they are rich people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהוּ, כֵּיוָן דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ לְאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's answer to the question in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The traveler has the status of an עני and may establish residence at a distant spot by speech ('במקום פלוני'). The townspeople have the status of עשירים and may not.

steps.title: Conclusion: naming a spot works for the poor, not the rich
steps.stepSummary: From this, the גמרא concludes that saying 'my resting place is at such-and-such spot' works for an עני but not for an עשיר. This proves רב נחמן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that any case of 'at such-and-such place' works for a poor man, but not for a rich man. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the final lesson from the משנה and confirms that רב נחמן is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה is רבי יהודה's view. Even he lets only the traveler, who counts as an עני, set his residence at a distant spot (במקום פלוני), while the townspeople, who count as עשירים, cannot. That matches רב נחמן, who said everyone (even רבי יהודה) agrees 'במקום פלוני' is only for an עני. It goes against רב חסדא, who said רבי יהודה allows 'במקום פלוני' even for an עשיר. 'שמע מינה' seals the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see / apparently
At such-and-such place (naming a resting spot by speech)
Learn from this (the proof stands)

steps.whatToRemember: Even according to רבי יהודה, naming a distant spot ('במקום פלוני') works only for an עני, meaning someone on the road. It does not work for an עשיר, meaning someone at home with food. This supports רב נחמן against רב חסדא. Saying 'במקומי' while standing at the spot is a separate case. There רבי יהודה allows even an עשיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of the verbal עירוב. Naming a distant spot is only for someone on the road. Standing at the spot and saying 'במקומי' is a separate case, and רב rules like רבי יהודה that it works for an עשיר too (step 21).

phrases.english: Apparently, every (case of) 'at such-and-such place' —
for a poor man, yes,
for a rich man, no.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא כָּל בְּמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי עָנִי אִין עָשִׁיר לָא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from רב הונא's explanation and closes רב אשי's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even according to רבי יהודה, naming a distant spot ('במקום פלוני') works for an עני (a traveler) but not for an עשיר. The משנה supports רב נחמן against רב חסדא.

steps.title: A student recites the משנה's line about rich and poor
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי teaches חייא בר רב the משנה's words 'both a poor person and a rich person,' in front of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי was teaching חייא בר רב, in front of רב, the line: 'both a poor person and a rich person.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene for a ruling. A teacher recites the line in the משנה where רבי יהודה says the walking עירוב works for an עני and an עשיר alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר limits the walking עירוב to an עני. רבי יהודה says it works for an עשיר too. This step only quotes רבי יהודה's words, so that רב can comment on them in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: was teaching (reciting the משנה to a student)
in front of רב
both a poor person and a rich person

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi was teaching
phrases.notes: He is reciting the משנה to a student.

phrases.english: to Chiyya, son of Rav, in front of Rav:
phrases.notes: רב, the student's father, was listening.

phrases.english: "Both a poor person and a rich person."
phrases.notes: These are רבי יהודה's words in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עני/עשיר discussion ends, the גמרא brings a scene of the משנה being taught. This scene leads into a final ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's line from רבי יהודה is quoted: the walking עירוב applies to both an עני and an עשיר.

steps.title: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב tells the student to add that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: End it off also with 'The הלכה follows רבי יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a practical ruling. When you recite רבי יהודה's words, you should add that the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רבי יהודה's view from one opinion in a מחלוקת into the practical הלכה. So the walking עירוב is not limited to an עני on the road. An עשיר may use it too.

keyTerms.meaning: conclude with it / add at the end
the practical law follows רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: רב rules like רבי יהודה: the walking עירוב works for both an עני and an עשיר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who says what. 'Both a poor person and a rich person' is רבי יהודה's view, and רב rules like him. רבי מאיר is the one who limits it to an עני.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling. It sets how widely the walking עירוב may be used on שבת.

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
Conclude it also with:
phrases.notes: Add a closing line to the recitation.

phrases.english: "The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda."

steps.triggerLanguage: סַיֵּים בָּהּ נָמֵי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב comments on the line that was just recited and adds a ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: the walking עירוב works for an עשיר as well as an עני.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, both an עני and an עשיר may set their שבת resting place by going to the spot and declaring 'במקומי', following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A story begins about רבה בר רב חנן's regular trip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a story: רבה בר רב חנן used to travel from ארטיבנא to פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן used to come regularly from ארטיבנא to פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new story. Nothing has happened yet; it only tells us that רבה בר רב חנן regularly made this trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Traveling between two towns on שבת brings up the rules of שבת limits and עירוב. The background fact here, that he made this trip regularly, prepares for the event or question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: was in the habit of / used to regularly
ארטיבנא, the town where רבה בר רב חנן lived
פומבדיתא, a major Babylonian Torah center

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן הֲוָה רְגִיל
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Chanan was in the habit
of coming from Artibna to Pumbedita.
phrases.notes: This refers to travel on שבת, which raises the rules of שבת limits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן הֲוָה רְגִיל דְּאָתֵי מֵאַרְטִיבְנָא לְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב's ruling, the גמרא moves to a real-life story about traveling on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background fact only: רבה בר רב חנן regularly traveled from ארטיבנא to פומבדיתא.
